memos.risk:
Risk call on NUVI: lean toward refusing, but if the desk insists, keep it minimal.

Refuse-by-default signals: the bundle share is 36.75%, a sign of coordinated buying. The coin is 48% off its 30-minute high after a 50% run-up, which looks like a blow-off. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is only +19.7 SOL against 780 SOL of sells, and sellers outnumber buyers (1,289 vs 1,653 buyers, with sells roughly equal to buys). The 2-minute post-graduation sell-to-buy ratio is about 1.0, meaning sellers matched buyers almost exactly.

Sizing if the desk buys anyway: $5 ticket (the minimum), 20% stop, 15-minute hold. The 122 SOL pool gives enough depth that $5 won't move the price much, but the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost plus the 30-second latency leave little room for a bad fill.

I would refuse any size above $5, or any buy if bundle share keeps rising or net flow turns negative.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying NUVI now is weak, so I'd lean toward skipping.

What supports demand: 1,653 buyers and 799.58 SOL bought in the last 15 minutes, with 823 curve buyers and only 4.4% of supply held by the top 3. The coin is alive, not airdrop-dumped, and classed ORGANIC, so the factory-coin penalty doesn't apply.

What argues against it: net flow over the last 15 minutes is just +19.68 SOL against 779.91 SOL sold, so nearly every buy was matched by a sell. The sell-to-buy ratio right after graduation was about 1.0, and the price is down 48% from its 30-minute high despite a 4% gain over the last 15 minutes. Bundling is high at 37% of curve share, and a launch bot was present. The shallow 123 SOL pool means a $20 round trip will cost at the high end of the 1.4-5.1% range. The name leans on a popular meme theme, which is data about the creator's intent, not evidence of staying power.

Demand is real in headcount but thin in net terms, and the sharp drawdown suggests the high was sold into. I don't see a case that demand will still be here in 30-60 minutes, so the recommendation is to skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: distribution into the bounce. NUVI is up 49.5% over 30 minutes, but it's 48% off its 30-minute high, and the last 15 minutes show net flow of only +19.7 SOL against 779.9 SOL sold, with 1,289 sellers versus 1,653 buyers. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes after graduation was 1.006, meaning early buyers were already exiting as fast as they entered. A bundle share of 36.8% and a launch bot point to coordinated early wallets that can keep distributing into any bid. With a 122.8 SOL pool, a $20 ticket would be about 0.16 SOL, and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost leaves little margin on a bounce that has already faded. Bundled and bot-assisted coins that have already retraced this far usually don't recover the dip. Skip.
